messages.author: 04e62c3b36bb17bf
messages.subject: BCsFt in R/qtl2
parts:
Hi Karl et al. 

I am analyzing QTL in a BC3F2 population. It appears that this cross design isn't really implemented in R/qtl2 yet. Would you recommend treating it as an F2, or just sticking to R/qtl?
Thanks,
John

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] BCsFt in R/qtl2
parts:
If you have high density genotypes and want to control for population structure using an LMM, you might want to try R/qtl2; otherwise you’d probably stick with R/qtl. You might also try calculating the genotype probabilities in R/qtl and then converting them to R/qtl2 format with the qtl2convert package, probs_qtl_to_qtl2(). 

karl

Thanks Karl - so you don't think there is a problem with qtl2::calc_genoprob or qtl2::scan1 for BCsFt populations treated as an F2? I do want to control for population structure, so R/qtl2 is optimal, I just want to make sure I'm not violating some critical assumptions.
Cheers,

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] BCsFt in R/qtl2
parts:
If very high density genotypes, I think it would be okay to assume F2 and use qtl2. But I would want to study results before making the decision, and I’d always prefer to do calculations with the “right” model.

karl
